newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Authorities in Bangkok are on red alert as the first wave of floodwater from the north is expected to reach the capital today, aggravating the situation in areas already submerged and flooding other parts of the city. Motorists have been warned to avoid a number of roads expected to be flooded by peak tides in the Chao Phraya river. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Chart Thai party says it is cleaning up its act by getting rid of unacceptable members in an attempt to improve the party's image. Key party members say that the mass defections to other parties by Chart Thai members who demanded political positions, will only work in Chart Thai's favour. (THE NATION)

- Four Democrat Party members, including party leader Chuan Leekpai, have been found not guilty of involvement in a land scandal in the southern resort island of Phuket. The investigation report submitted recently by Phuket police to the provincial prosecution excluded the four from the list of 18 suspects accused of falsifying their land ownership statements. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has stressed that he would let a new government deal with the issuance of licences for new domestic banking and insurance companies. He says that he never forced former finance minister Bodi Chunnananda to endorse the licences. (MANAGER)

- Thailand's first National Tourism Master Plan, due out next year, will focus on strategies to boost the tourism industry by considering environmental preservation equally with financial benefit. The environmentally-based promotion plan will be formally implemented beginning in the 1998 fiscal year. (THE NATION)

- Nine firms seeking stock market listings have asked the Stock Exchange of Thailand to defer plans to divest shares to the general public. The calls were made as the SET index continued to fall yesterday. (BANGKOK POST)

- The appointment of Chayawat Wibulswadi as acting finance minister failed to boost the bourse which slid to a fresh three-year low on continued off-loading of banking and finance shares. (BUSINESS DAY)
